findings.text: In Isa 57:15 and 1 Sam 16:7, both marked by the M08 strand's group B scan, the height word is not pride: it supports M47 (heart, spirit). findings.text: A heart that cannot be quiet: the wicked are like the tossing sea, for it cannot be quiet, and its waters toss up mire and dirt; there is no peace, says my God, for the wicked (Isa 57:20-21). This is the figure of an inner state: restless, unable to be still, throwing up what is in it. The book already has the arrogant man never at rest (Hab 2:5) and the quieted soul of Psalm 131, but not this picture.

findings.text: 1 Sam 16:6 holds the seer's own thought, formed from what he saw: when they came, he looked on Eliab and thought, Surely the Lord's anointed is before him. The rebuke in 16:7 (man looks on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart) answers that thought: even the prophet, sent by God to choose, made up his mind from the outside. The book quotes the principle but not the mistake it corrects.
